questions.q: If a set contains $n$ elements, then its power set will contain
questions.solution:
Let there is only& $1$~element in a set~$S$, and let~$S = \left\{a\right\}$.

So, power set of~$S\text{is}P\left(S\right) = \left\{ϕ, \left\{a\right\}\right\}$.~

Which shows that number of elements contained in the power set are~$2 = {2}^{1}$.~

Similarly,~if there are~$2$~elements in a set~$S$,~and let~$S = \left\{a, b\right\}$.

So, power set of~$S\text{is}P\left(S\right) = \left\{ϕ, \left\{a\right\}, \left\{b\right\}, \left\{a, b\right\}\right\}$.

Which shows that number of elements contained in the power set are~${2}^{2} .$~

Similarly,~if there are~$n$~elements in a~set~$S$,~then the number of elements in the power set of~$S$~will be~$= {2}^{n} .$

questions.q: A class has 175 students. The following data shows the number of students opting for one or more subjects. Mathematics 100; Physics 70; Chemistry 40; Mathematics and Physics 30; Mathematics and Chemistry 28; Physics and Chemistry 23; Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry 18. How& many students have offered Mathematics alone?
questions.solution:
Given, $n\left(M\right) = 100, n\left(P\right) = 70, n\left(C\right) = 40$

$n\left(M ∩ P\right) = 30, n\left(M ∩ C\right) = 28,$

$n\left(P ∩ C\right) = 23$ and $n\left(M ∩ P ∩ C\right) = 18$

$∴ n\left(M ∩ P^{′} ∩ C^{′}\right) = n [ M ∩ ( P ∪ C)^{'} ]$

$= n\left(M\right) - [ n\left(M ∩ P\right) + n\left(M ∩ C\right) - n ( M ∩ P ∩ C ) ]$

$= 100 - [ 30 + 28 - 18 ] = 60$

Then $n$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{30}n\left(Ai\right) = 5 \times 30 = 150$

Let $S$ consist of $m$~distinct elements. Since each elements of $S$ belongs to exactly $10$ of the $Ai^{'}$,~so,~we~have& $\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{30}n\left({A}_{i}\right) = 10m = 150 ⇒ m = 15$

Now each ${B}_{i}$ has $3$ elements and each elements of $S$ belongs to exactly $9$ of the ${B}_{i}$'s.~So, we have~$\mathop{∑}_{j = 1}^{n}n\left({B}_{j}\right) = 3n = 9m ⇒ 3n = 9 \times 15 ⇒ n = 45$

questions.q: 205 students take an examination of whom 105 pass in English, 70 students pass in Mathematics and 30 students pass in both. How many students fail in both subjects?
questions.solution: Total number of students $=205$ Number of students passed in Math $=70$ Number of students passed in English $=105$ and number of students pass in both $=30$ Now, Number of students passed in Math or English. = Number of students passed in Math + Number of student passed in English - Number of students passed in both $=70+105-30=145$ So, number of students fail in both subjects $=$ Total number of students - Students passed in Math or English $=205-145=60$

questions.q: Let $P$ be the relation defined on the set of all real numbers such that $\text{P} = \left\{\left(\text{a, b}\right) \text{:} \sec^{2} \text{a} - \tan^{2} \text{b} = 1\right\}$. Then $P$ is
options: reflexive and symmetric but not transitive
symmetric and transitive but not reflexive
reflexive and transitive but not symmetric
questions.solution:
$\text{P} = \left\{\left(\text{a, b}\right) \text{:} \sec^{2} \text{a} - \tan^{2} \text{b} = 1\right\}$

$\sec^{2} \text{a} - \tan^{2} \text{b} = 1$

$⇒ \sec^{2} \text{a} = 1 + \tan^{2} \text{b}$

$⇒ \sec^{2} \text{a} = \sec^{2} \text{b}$

$⇒ \left|\text{sec a}\right| = \left|\text{sec b}\right|$

$\sec^{2} \text{a} - \tan^{2} \text{b} = 1$

$1 + \tan^{2} \text{a} - \sec^{2} \text{b} + 1 = 1$

$\sec^{2} \text{b} - \tan^{2} \text{a} = 1$

Hence, it is Symmetric.

If \left|\text{sec a}\right| = \left|\text{sec b}\right|$ and \left|\text{sec b}\right| = \left|\text{sec c}\right|$ then \left|\text{sec a}\right| = \left|\text{sec c}\right| ⇒$ transitive

So it is an equivalence relation.

$⇒$ The required number of elements $( a, b ) = 12$

questions.question: The number of elements in the set $\left\{\left(a, b\right): {a}^{2} + {b}^{2} = 50; a, b \in Z\right\}$, where $Z$ is the set of all integers, is
questions.explanation:
${a}^{2} + {b}^{2} = 50$
$a = 1 ⇒ {b}^{2} = 49$
$⇒ b = \pm 7$
$a = 2, 3, 4, 6$ do not give integer value of $b$ .
$a = 5 ⇒ {b}^{2} = 25 ⇒ b = \pm 5$
$a = 7 ⇒ {b}^{2} = 1$
$⇒ b = \pm 1$
Similarly,
$a = - 1 ⇒ b = \pm 7$
$a = - 5 ⇒ b = \pm 5$
$a = - 7 \to b = \pm 1$
$⇒$ The required number of elements $( a, b ) = 12$

questions.q: Let $S$ be the set of all real numbers. Then, the relation $R = { \left(a, b\right): 1 + ab > 0 }$ on $S$ is
options: reflexive and symmetric but not transitive
reflexive and transitive but not symmetric
questions.solution:
$R = { \left(a, b\right): 1 + ab > 0 }$
(i) $( 1, 1 ) \in R$

(ii) $( 1, 2 ) \in \mathbb{R} ⇒ ( 2, 1 ) \in R$

(iii) $( 1, 2 ) \in Rand ( 2, 3 ) \in \mathbb{R} ⇒ ( 1, 3 ) \in R$
It is clear that the given relation on $S$ is reflexive, symmetric but not transitive.

questions.q: If in a class there are $200$ students in which $120$ take Mathematics, $90$ take Physics, $60$ take Chemistry, $50$ take Mathematics & Physics, $50$ take Mathematics & Chemistry, $43$ take Physics & Chemistry and $38$ take Mathematics, Physics & Chemistry, then the number of students who have taken exactly one subject is
questions.solution:
Let, $M \to$Mathematics, $P \to$Physics, $C \to$Chemistry
Given that total students $= 200$
$n\left(M\right) = 120,n\left(P\right) = 90, n\left(C\right) = 60$
$n\left(M ∩ P\right) = 50,n\left(M ∩ C\right) = 50, n\left(P ∩ C\right) = 43$
$n\left(M ∩ P ∩ C\right) = 38$
Required number of students taking exactly one subject is
$n\left(M\right) + n\left(P\right) + n \left($C\right) - 2n \left(M ∩ P\right) - 2n \left($P ∩ C\right) - $2n\left($M ∩ C\right) + $3n\left($M ∩ P ∩ C\right)$
$= 120 + 90 + 60 - 2 \left(50\right) - 2 \left($50\right) - $2\left($43\right) + $3\left($38\right)$
$= 98
